Read returns raw file lines — SymbolBody returns the same range with structural awareness (used imports, refs, declared kind) at the same or lower token cost. Use:
  • SymbolOutline(target="app/big.py") — file structure, no bodies
  • SymbolBody(target="<qualified.path>") — one named symbol + imports + refs
  • SymbolBody(target="app/big.py:START-END") — arbitrary line range with refs
Read only when you genuinely need the unstructured file content (top-level comments, module-level constants, or non-code regions)."}}

Write would overwrite it wholesale, losing the per-symbol structural edit guarantees. For changes to an existing indexed file, use:
  • Patch(file=..., range=A-B, content=...) — byte-range edit, atomic
  • ReplaceSymbol(qualified_path=..., content=...) — whole symbol; parse-validated
  • InsertSymbol(anchor=..., position=..., content=...) — structural insert
Write is correct only for *new* files (it's a no-op nudge in that case)."}}

{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "allow", "additionalContext": "symbol: "app/big.py" is indexed (python). Edit requires re-sending the existing content for disambiguation (~200 extra tokens per call) and provides no parse validation. The MCP write tools cover every case Edit covers:
  • Patch(file=..., range=A-B, content=...) — byte-range, no old_string round-trip (handles ALL non-symbol edits)
  • ReplaceSymbol(qualified_path=..., content=...) — whole symbol; parse-validated; rewrites callers if leaf renamed
  • InsertSymbol(anchor=..., position=before|after|start|end, content=...) — auto-indented, structural
  • DeleteSymbol(qualified_path=...) — refuses if callers exist
  • RenameSymbol(qualified_path=..., new_name=...) — atomic across files, transactional (Undo-able)
Use Edit only on files symbol does not index."}}
